questions.q: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio equals the opposite divided by the hypotenuse?
A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 10 and an angle of 30°. The opposite side equals 10 × sin 30°. What is its length?
What is the value of sin 90°?
questions.explain: sin 90° = 1 is a standard exact value.

questions.q: To find a missing angle when you know the opposite and adjacent sides, which is used?
questions.explain: With opposite and adjacent you use tan, then inverse tan to get the angle.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs 5 and 12. What is the hypotenuse?
tan x = 1, where x is between 0° and 90°. What is the angle x?
What is the exact value of cos 60°?
questions.explain: cos 60° = 1/2 is a standard exact value.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has both shorter sides given but no angle. To find the third side you use:
questions.explain: With no angle and two sides, Pythagoras' theorem finds the third side.

questions.q: What is the exact value of sin 30°?
questions.explain: sin 30° = 1/2 is a standard exact value.

questions.explain: East corresponds to a bearing of 090° measured clockwise from North.
